conceptTest: Psycholinguistics provides a direct course in language perception, production, acquisition and impairment. Stylistics, textual interpretation, cognitive neuroscience, experiments, statistics, qualitative inquiry and text modelling provide sustained supporting directions. The option remains provisional pending comparator progression evidence.

candidateTests.structural: Formal logic supplies notation and proof, stylistics analyses grammar and meaning in texts, and beginner Dutch supplies language practice. Those courses cannot sustain linguistic phonology, morphology, syntax or formal semantics and pragmatics. Literature and rhetoric would give adjacent interpretation, not a second distinct structural curriculum.
candidateTests.clinical: Psycholinguistics includes aphasia and dyslexia. Cognitive neuroscience, lifespan psychology and clinical interviewing support related knowledge, but no sustained sequence teaches clinical language assessment, differential diagnosis, specialist neuroimaging or therapy. General neurobiology and health psychology do not substitute for that clinical sequence. Adding more clinical general psychology would not support a distinct linguistic option.

academicConstruction: Psycholinguistics moves from term six to its sole planned term two, after Brain & Behavior. Rhetoric in Action moves from term four to term six. Added programming, logic, machine learning, AI ethics and qualitative methods to deepen language study; removed beginner Dutch, film and media and other less direct content. Retained at least six 300-level courses. Removed alignments equating general development, rhetoric and textual stylistics with dedicated acquisition, pragmatics and semantics, and avoided implying introductory brain and behaviour is language neuroimaging. AI Ethics has a documented direct part in common with the humane AI course. Psycholinguistics and Statistics comparisons remain provisional.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Literature use, academic writing, research questions and reflective learning provide general academic formation.

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.contribution: Uses ethical and psychological frameworks to examine privacy, fairness and responsibility in AI.

DISARIN212.name: Logic & Discrete Mathematics
DISARIN212.contribution: Uses formal logic, sets and relations to build analytical foundations for studying structure and meaning.

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: Cleans, joins, analyses and visualises data, including text, in R.

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: Evaluates classification and prediction methods on held-out datasets, supporting later text modelling.

DISDATA311.name: Neural Networks & Deep Learning
DISDATA311.contribution: Implements and evaluates neural networks, with work on text prediction and transformers.

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: Writes and tests Python programs with functions and data structures for later computational text work.

DISGATE102.name: Mathematical Methods
DISGATE102.contribution: Builds mathematical modelling and optimisation foundations for later machine-learning work.

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: Designs qualitative research using interviews, observations and systematic interpretation of qualitative evidence.

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: Examines nervous systems, brain anatomy and comparative methods for studying behaviour.

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: Studies sensory processing and goal-directed behaviour using cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: Uses cognitive experiments and research design to study attention, memory and higher functions involved in language processing.

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: Directly studies speech comprehension, production, acquisition, bilingualism, aphasia and dyslexia and uses experimental approaches to language processing.

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: Introduces the brain, behaviour, learning and behavioural and imaging methods used in cognitive science.

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: Examines social cognition and influence, including how the presence and behaviour of others affect communication.

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: Uses experimental design, multivariable models and R to analyse behavioural evidence.

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: Studies clinical communication, interviewing and the psychological and social effects of health conditions.

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: Uses systematic review and meta-analysis to compare evidence and effect sizes across behavioural studies.

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: Examines cognitive and social development across the lifespan using theories, cases and an interview.

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: Analyses how arguments, delivery and rhetorical choices affect audiences.

MCCCOMM211.name: Style & Meaning
MCCCOMM211.contribution: Uses grammar, modality, deixis and discourse to explain how linguistic choices shape meaning in texts.

MCCCOMM213.name: Rhetoric in Action
MCCCOMM213.contribution: Applies and adapts oral storytelling, public speaking and debate activities for school pupils.

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: Uses framing, verbal and nonverbal communication, and argumentation to evaluate persuasive messages.

MCCLITR111.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
MCCLITR111.contribution: Uses close reading, genre and form to investigate how textual choices create meaning.

alignment.rationale: Both address language processing and experimental psycholinguistics. Groningen devotes a separate course to a psycholinguistics project.
Both examine applications of AI alongside ethics and effects on people and society. Groningen also studies language, multimodality and AI literacy.
Both support empirical research using statistical analysis. UCR applies multivariable models and experimental methods to behavioural research.
